title: A Frank!Framework adapter is the highest-leverage demo on the list because it ships inside 10,000+ live integrations
content:
The Frank!Framework is Apache-2.0 licensed and, per the research, already runs more than 10,000 integrations in production. The demo is a single adapter inside it, contributed back upstream, that dispatches one typed operation per exchange. Every message the framework moves then leaves a record of what that exchange decided.

The leverage comes from where the code lands. A client integration reaches one deployment; an adapter merged into the framework travels with every installation that takes the upgrade. The research calls this the highest-leverage demo on the whole list for exactly that reason — the distribution belongs to the framework, and contributing back under the framework's own licence is the price of admission rather than a concession made along the way.

The same fact constrains the design. Because the adapter ships to everyone, it has to satisfy the framework's maintainers rather than one client's requirements, which makes this a framework contribution with an upstream review to pass, not a bespoke build that can be shaped freely.
